operativeSourceText:
Section 1.01 of the Credit Agreement is
hereby amended by adding the following definitions in the appropriate alphabetical order:
“Invoice
Restrictions” has the meaning set forth in the Monthly Factoring Report.
“Maintenance Liquidity”
means, as of any date of determination, (a) the sum as of such date of (x) the aggregate amount of the commitments under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility (including the aggregate revolving commitments with respect to any
Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness) (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) minus (y) the aggregate principal amount of the outstanding revolving loans under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility and any
outstanding revolving loans in respect of any Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) and, in each case, the face amount of any letters of credit issued thereunder (less any reimbursed amounts)
plus (b) the “Adjustment to Liquidity” as set forth in the most recently delivered Monthly Factoring Report plus (c) unrestricted cash and Cash Equivalents of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries.

“Monthly Factoring Report” means a report substantially in
the form of Exhibit E or any other form approved by the Administrative Agent.

findings.irPath: definitions[1].calculationExpression.operands[0].left... (SUBTRACT right operand, third-level ADD operand: 'Face amount of letters of credit issued... less any reimbursed amounts')
findings.sourceEvidence: "and, in each case, the face amount of any letters of credit issued thereunder (less any reimbursed amounts)"
findings.proposedIrEvidence: {"kind":"METRIC_REFERENCE","metricName":"Face amount of letters of credit issued under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility and any Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness (or Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof), less any reimbursed amounts"}
findings.verifierReasoning: The source expresses a genuine subtraction: the LC face amount is reduced by any reimbursed amounts before being combined with outstanding loans to form component (y). The proposed IR does not model this as a computable SUBTRACT node; instead it folds 'less any reimbursed amounts' into descriptive prose inside a single METRIC_REFERENCE node's metricName. If the downstream metric-resolution system does not itself already net out reimbursements when resolving this named metric, the formula tree as structured provides no mechanism to perform that subtraction, which could cause Maintenance Liquidity to be overstated (LC face amount not reduced for reimbursements). This is a plausible, though not certain, loss of operative formula structure - I cannot confirm from the evidence given whether the metric-resolution layer independently guarantees the netting, so I mark this UNCERTAIN rather than definitively MATERIAL.

findings.sourceEvidence: "the aggregate amount of the commitments under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility (including the aggregate revolving commitments with respect to any Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness) ... minus (y) the aggregate principal amount of the outstanding revolving loans under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility..."
findings.proposedIrEvidence: "instrumentKey": "sup-term-loan-instrument" (used on every METRIC_REFERENCE node in this definition, including the commitments, outstanding revolving loans, LC face amount, Adjustment to Liquidity, and unrestricted cash metrics)
findings.verifierReasoning: Every metric in this definition is explicitly tied by the source text to the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility (a revolving facility) or to unencumbered borrower/subsidiary cash - none of it concerns a term loan. Yet every METRIC_REFERENCE node in the proposed IR carries instrumentKey 'sup-term-loan-instrument', which by its name suggests a term-loan instrument rather than the revolving facility described in the source. If this key is used by the downstream system to resolve which instrument's outstanding balances/commitments to pull at evaluation time, using a term-loan instrument key here could cause Maintenance Liquidity to be computed from the wrong facility's data entirely, materially distorting the liquidity figure. I cannot rule out that this is simply an internal deal-level identifier unrelated to facility type (in which case it would be immaterial), so I mark this UNCERTAIN rather than confirmed MATERIAL, but it is a real naming inconsistency worth review.
